title: Tilt and Tether Hiring + Pricing Probe (Sprint edition)
summary: One-page tactical workbook to evaluate short-window hiring adjustments (tilt) versus pricing nudges (tether) under four demand shock scenarios. Focused on near-term runway protection, SLA risk, and token-unit economics impact. Intended for finance + product ops decision in the next 6–12 week cadence.
purpose_and_scope: Build a small, actionable matrix that treasury/ops can use to decide whether to pause hires, slow offers, or introduce micro-pricing changes (volume discounts, temporary premium) during demand swings. Not a replacement for the quarter plan — a sprint-level guardrail.
key_assumptions: Baseline ARR growth: 35% YoY; Hosted API average tokens per call: 420; Avg revenue per 1M tokens: $160; Dedicated contract uplift: 3.6x hosted margin; Hiring lead time (SWE/Infra): 8 weeks; Contractor ramp: 3 weeks; Burst GPU spot cost multiplier: 1.25x.

sensitivity_analysis_notes: We model four demand scenarios across price and hiring levers. Key metric: months-to-runway at 18% margin floor and token cost per 1k tokens. Secondary metric: % of requests meeting 200ms p95 latency given current dedicated capacity. The tuning knobs are: immediate hiring freeze (stop all new reqs), 50% hiring slowdown (only critical roles), small price lift (+8% hosted API), and micro-discount gating (volume discount threshold raised).

risk_notes:
- Hiring freeze increases backlog risk: two-week sprint predictability falls 25% and increases customer escalations.
- Price increases risk churn in SMB self-serve cohort; early telemetry should monitor churn in first 30 days post-change.
- Discount threshold gating could push high-volume developers to competitors; communicate as targeted experiment.
- Operational risk: contractor reliance increases support costs and knowledge debt.
recommended_next_steps:
1) Approve Hybrid experiment for 8 weeks (slow hiring + +4% hosted price).
2) Instrument churn and activation cohort signals; daily publish to console channel.
3) Freeze non-critical non-customer-facing feature work and reallocate infra hires to KV-cache + batching improvements.
4) Prepare comms docs for enterprise accounts (exceptions process).
5) Re-evaluate after 6 weeks and either roll back or escalate to Q1 planning.
